Title: Efficacy and safety of live varicella zoster vaccine in diabetes: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
Author: Hata et al.
Comment: The paper did not report a risk ratio or confidence interval, so these fields are left null. Design Type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group clinical trial
Study Environment: Single-centre trial at Kitano Hospital, a general hospital in Osaka
Topic of Content: Adverse experiences after live attenuated Oka varicella zoster vaccination

Title: Safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity of zoster vaccine in subjects with a history of herpes zoster
Author: Mills et al.
Comment: Crossover analysis summarized observations by clinical material received rather than as independent parallel arms. Table percentages use subjects with follow-up (98 ZOSTAVAX and 96 placebo), while Table 2 explicitly reports 100 and 101 as the respective numbers of subjects; per the synthesis contract, the latter were used as totals. The paper reports risk differences as its planned comparison but does not provide a risk-difference value for this row and does not report an RR, so no effect estimate was entered.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('ZOSTAVAX') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover multicenter trial
Content length: 28-day post-vaccination safety follow-up after each injection
Topic of Content: Live attenuated herpes zoster vaccine safety in adults with prior herpes zoster
Participant type: Healthy adults aged 50 years or older with a physician-documented history of herpes zoster at least 5 years before study entry
Outcome measurement: Participants with one or more adverse experiences of any type during days 1–28 post-vaccination
effect_direction: RR > 1 indicates more participants experienced an adverse event with vaccine than with placebo

Report_ID: With one or more AE (Days 0–42 postvaccination 1)
Title: Safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity after 1 and 2 doses of zoster vaccine in healthy adults 60 years of age
Author: Vermeulen et al.
Comment: The paper does not report a risk ratio for this outcome; retain the verbatim event counts and totals for downstream RR calculation. This is the first of two repeated 42-day safety windows in the same randomized participants and is not independent of the postvaccination-2 result.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Zoster vaccine') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: Six clinical sites (5 United States; 1 Netherlands)
Topic of Content: Occurrence of any adverse experience after live zoster vaccination
Participant type: Healthy adults aged 60 years or older
Outcome measurement: Subjects recorded injection-site and/or systemic adverse experiences on a standardized Vaccination Report Card for 42 days after vaccination.
Outcome variable: With one or more AE (Days 0–42 postvaccination 1)
effect_direction: RR > 1 indicates more participants experienced an adverse event with vaccine than with placebo

Title: A Vaccine to Prevent Herpes Zoster and Postherpetic Neuralgia in Older Adults
Author: Oxman et al.
Comment: Table 4 states that percentages other than death and hospitalization are weighted in proportion to the number of subjects with safety follow-up in each age group; therefore, the displayed percentages may not equal the raw event counts divided by the displayed substudy totals. Raw reported counts and substudy denominators were extracted for RR synthesis.
